- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp spike in sentiment or price, model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 20–40% for 2–4 days post-spike.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if forecast is >2.5σ above recent mean, reduce by 15–30% for next 5 days; if <2.5σ below, increase by 15–30%.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; apply a 10–15% dampening factor if sentiment volatility >0.5 in last 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to drift toward zero; apply a “baseline correction” to avoid underestimating near-zero sentiment periods.
